svg.font-family: Segoe UI, Inter, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: WDAC POLICY REBASE
svg.desc: The rebase replaces the App Control base policy on a PAW with a new Wizard baseline that has both Recommended Block Rules boxes unchecked, deployed locally without GPO. Steps 0 to 2 back up the device, take it out of GPO scope and build the new baseline. Steps 3 to 7 validate it and swap the base policy in Audit, either with a new GUID (Route A: remove the old policy, re-create its supplementals; every step documented by Microsoft) or by keeping the GUID (Route B: an undocumented XML edit, then an in-place replacement). Steps 8 and 9 capture every application again, merge and screen, then enforce and verify V-243450 and V-243451.
svg.text: APP CONTROL FOR BUSINESS · NEW BASELINE · NO RECOMMENDED BLOCK RULES · LOCAL · NO GPO · ROUTE A OR ROUTE B
WINDOWS 11 22H2+ · UNSIGNED POLICY · CITOOL · PS 7 OR 5.1
backup in C:\WDAC\Backups\Rebase-<timestamp> · scripts in C:\WDAC-Scripts · both block-list boxes unchecked

g.text: Make the change reversible, take the device away from the GPO, and
Move the computer out of the WDAC GPOs' OU
gpupdate: AppControl GPO and WDAC-GPO-Deploy task gone
The old .cip stays on the device until step 5 or 6
[Wizard] Allow Microsoft, Multiple Policy Format, Audit ON
Both Merge with Recommended Block Rules boxes UNCHECKED
A GPO still in scope redeploys its policy: Route A would end with two base
Validate the new baseline and put it in place of the old base policy, in
2 x WARN: no deny rules in scenario 12 / 131 = boxes unchecked
6: scripts 1 + 2 deploy the baseline, new GUID
ROUTE B · KEEP GUID · NOT DOCUMENTED
3: write the old GUID into Base-Audit.xml (XML edit)
6: scripts 1 + 2 replace the policy in place
CRITICAL · ROUTE B STEP 3 IS UNDOCUMENTED
No cmdlet sets a chosen GUID. Microsoft recommends the Wizard or ConfigCI
Capture every application again on the new baseline, then enforce
Reboot, run EVERY app: earlier allow rules are gone
Reboot, approved apps run, block-test app gets 3077
CRITICAL · NEVER MERGE THE OLD REFERENCE
The old Base-Enforce.xml and Base-Audit-Merged.xml hold the block rules.
Merging them brings the rules back.

svg.text: New Base-Audit.xml (no block rules) → Base-Audit-Merged.xml → Base-Enforce.xml
Old files stay in the Step 0 backup · after the swap, every revision keeps the new baseline's GUID and raises VersionEx
pick one route before step 3 · what keeps the rebase safe
Route A (new GUID) or Route B (keep the GUID)
both end the same: one base policy in Audit, rebuilt, then enforced

g.text: Step 5: CiTool -rp the old base + supplementals
Step 7: supplementals re-created for the new base
Script 1 writes the new GUID to PolicyGuid.txt
Step 3: old GUID into the new XML (XML edit)
Script 1 picks a HIGHER version: in-place swap
Move the computer object out of the WDAC OU
gpupdate removes the task; the .cip stays
Don't disable the GPOs: other devices use them
User mode: Microsoft-signed bypass tools now allowed
e.g. msbuild, mshta, wmic, wsl; -AllowWSL not needed
Kernel mode: Windows' own driver blocklist still on
User mode (V-243451) gives the mode: 1 = AUDIT
Kernel mode often reads 2 from built-in policies
CiTool IsEnforced = True means active, not enforce
Enforced, need Audit: README §11 Option A
Back to GPO: A removes the new base; B needs a higher package

svg.text: C:\WDAC\config · app control for business · policy rebase · 2026
